newsitem.title: USA: Taxol-treated ovarian cancer patients show benefit.
newsitem.headline: Taxol-treated ovarian cancer patients show benefit.

text.p: Patients with advanced ovarian cancer who were treated in a study with Taxol and cisplatin survive longer before their disease progresses, a meeting of oncologists in Denver, Colo., was told Tuesday.

The results of the study conducted in Europe and Canada were disclosed by Martine Piccart, a doctor who coordinated the study, before the 33rd annual meeting of the American Society of Clinical Oncology.
A report of Piccart's presentation was released by the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC).
Taxol is a yew tree extract the synthetic version of which is registered to Bristol-Myers Squibb Co, while cisplatin is used in ovarian-tumor therapy.
According to Piccart, the latest trial on Taxol combination therapy reaffirmed some of the benefits shown in a previous trial, known as GOG-111, of the same therapy.
The latest trial, known as Inter-Group Study, included 680 patients, lasted for 16 months and compared Taxol-cisplatin with a cisplatin-cyclophosphamide combination, Piccart said.

Results show that the ovarian cancer in patients who were given the Taxol combination did not progress for 16.6 months, compared with 12 months for those who received cisplatin plus cyclophosphamide, he said.

Piccart said the study, in contrast to GOG-111, recruited a very broad range of patients, including those with ovarian cancer in earlier stages, who previously had as much of as possible of their tumor removed surgically.

Piccart said that final analysis of the data from the trial will provide important information on the effects of the treatment on the quality of life experienced by patients, its cost effectiveness and survival.
"At this time, a final survival analysis has not been possible in the Inter-Group study because of the low number of deaths," Piccart noted.
